title: The Loose Safehouse
premise: Silas Eastwick, a former financial-crimes analyst turned whistle-blower living under four names in Rotterdam, has one rule: never get attached, never get noticed. When a private flight carrying Anton Varga — a defector holding proof that a cartel of banks laundered billions — vanishes from every tracking system midair, Silas is recognized by a handler she betrayed years ago and coerced into the extraction. As she moves Varga across Europe ahead of the Frankfurt market open, she discovers he is deliberate bait, dangled to flush out every whistle-blower the cartel has failed to silence. Silas chooses loyalty to the makeshift team she's gathered over the safe anonymity she's built, exposing the flight's true manifest at the opening bell and vanishing one last time — this time not alone, and not hiding.
about_author: Cyrus Nystrom is the pen name of a former logistics consultant who spent a decade moving sensitive cargo across European borders before turning to fiction. He writes in the margins of flight schedules and has never once checked a bag.

chapters.title: Four Names, One Bag
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. We meet her morning ritual: checking exits, rotating identities, keeping the go-bag by the door in a Rotterdam safehouse. A routine errand turns wrong when she spots a surveillance pattern she herself once taught an agency trainee. Emotional beat: the loneliness of a life built on leaving — and the first tremor that someone is closing in.

chapters.title: Ghost at Thirty-Seven Thousand Feet
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Silas watching news feeds; a brief interlude from air-traffic controller Mireille Kovač, who watches flight VX-221 vanish from every screen while passengers' phones keep transmitting. Emotional beat: uncanny dread — the modern world's systems don't fail, they are made to fail.

chapters.title: The Handler's Debt
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Odile Ferrant, the handler Silas burned six years ago, finds her and offers a devil's trade: help extract Varga from a private airfield outside Vienna, and Odile buries Silas's old file. Emotional beat: resentment and fear — Silas recognizes she was never hidden, only shelved.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wanted to Be Caught
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. At the airfield, the extraction goes too smoothly. Varga is calm, almost rehearsed, and his briefcase is lighter than his dossier claims. Silas notices the hangar cameras were angled to capture their faces. Emotional beat: the cold click of realizing she is inside someone else's trap.

chapters.title: Convoy of Strangers
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV, shifting between Silas, driver Tomas Beck, and Varga on the road to Frankfurt. A cartel kill team clips their tail; Tomas — a stranger hired that morning — takes a bullet and keeps driving. Emotional beat: the fragile, accidental birth of a found family under fire.

chapters.title: What Varga Carries
chapters.summary: Varga's POV, first time. He reveals the ledger is real but incomplete — the final page names the whistle-blowers, and the cartel wants them gathered in one place. He volunteered as bait to get that page out. Emotional beat: guilt and grim resolve; Silas must decide whether his honesty is courage or a second trap.

chapters.title: The Safehouse That Wasn't Safe
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. The team shelters in a secondary safehouse Silas has never used — and finds it already staged, down to her brand of tea. Odile is compromised or complicit; a listening device hums in the wall. Emotional beat: betrayal cutting deepest where trust was rationed most carefully.

chapters.title: Ledger of Names
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Wounded and sidelined, Tomas deciphers the ledger's final page and finds Silas's original name — plus Mireille's, and eleven others. He reaches Silas before Odile's people do. Emotional beat: loyalty chosen over survival; the moment Silas stops planning her exit.

chapters.title: Opening Bell
chapters.summary: Silas and Varga's POV, interleaved. At the Frankfurt exchange, they don't run — they broadcast. Mireille restores the vanished flight's transponder archive; the true manifest, with the cartel's beneficiaries, hits the tape as markets open. Odile arrives with a gun and, at the last second, chooses her old debt over her new masters. Emotional beat: catharsis — truth as a weapon fired in daylight.

chapters.title: The Fifth Name
chapters.summary: Silas's POV, weeks later. The cartel's lieutenants are indicted; Varga testifies under protection; Mireille rebuilds her life in the open. Silas retires her fourth name and, for the first time, unpacks the go-bag. Emotional beat: quiet resolution — she stops being a ghost and becomes a person, with a family that found her.
